subject: Unit economics deep-dive & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechx.com>, Jamie Olson <jamie.olson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Unit economics deep-dive & next steps

Hi Alex and Jamie,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the detailed walkthrough of FintechX's roadmap and the list of features that will use our inference API. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Recap of what's in scope from your side
   - Account verification workflow (high volume, short prompts)
   - Transaction-classification model for AML screening (medium volume, longer prompts)
   - In-product assistant for customer support (chat, higher state, session-based)

2) We need the following to build a tight unit-economics model (ideally before our deep-dive call):
   - Expected monthly token volumes by feature (input + output) — ballpark ranges are fine (e.g., 1M-5M).
   - Target cost envelope / budget range for inference (monthly or per-feature).
   - Any hard SLA/latency targets (p95 target, SLOs).

3) Next steps
   - Alex: can you share the token-volume estimates and rough budget range? If you prefer, a single spreadsheet with columns: feature, est monthly calls, est tokens/call (in/out), target $/month.
   - We'll use that to run a unit-econ model (redwood_unit_econ_template.xlsx attached) and return a $/1M tokens estimate plus recommended model variants / quantization profiles.
   - Proposed deep-dive call: Wed 24 Jun, 10:00-11:00 PT — will cover CAC payback scenarios, $/feature cost, and margin sensitivity. Let me know if that works.

Attaching our unit-econ template and a draft SOW for timeline/comments.

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- redwood_unit_econ_template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2 sheets: token assumptions, cost model)
- SOW-draft.pdf (draft scope & timeline)
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Jamie Olson <jamie.olson@fintechx.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive & next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick responses below and attached a lightweight spreadsheet with our initial estimates.

Token volume estimates (rough):
- Account verification: 2.5M tokens/month (mostly short prompts, avg 40 tokens in, 20 tokens out)
- Transaction-classification (AML): 1.2M tokens/month (avg 120 tokens in, 40 tokens out)
- In-product assistant (pilot): 750k tokens/month (avg 220 in, 160 out; ~35 sessions/day for pilot)

Budget / cost envelope
- Initial budget for inference: $10k-$25k/month depending on model options (we can expand if ROI is strong after pilot).

SLA: p95 latency target ~300ms for verification; AML is less strict (p95 ~600ms).

Open Qs for your deep-dive:
- Can you model both a hosted API (pay as you go) vs dedicated reserved capacity (committed throughput) for 12-month payback scenarios?
- We'd like a target that maps to $/1M tokens and also to $/feature for product-level ROI.

I'll be on the Wed 24 Jun slot proposed — works for me. Jamie will confirm.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product
FintechX
alex.rivera@fintechx.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechx.com>, Jamie Olson <jamie.olson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive & next steps

Great data — thanks Alex. Attached updated template filled with your numbers (redwood_unit_econ_template.xlsx) and a couple of scenarios we'll review on the call. High-level notes for the deep-dive: 

- We'll produce: 
  * $/1M tokens for each feature under hosted API vs dedicated capacity, with recommended model variant (open model vs optimized Redwood variant) and quantization option.
  * $/feature = (tokens/month * $/1M tokens scaled) + infra+ops allocation (we'll show sensitivity).
  * CAC payback examples: using your pilot assumptions, we'll show months-to-payback under conservative / base / aggressive conversion assumptions.

- Example targets to calibrate to: many fintech customers aim for <$500 per $1M tokens for low-latency verification flows on hosted; for higher quality multi-turn assistants that target may be $1,500-$3,000 per $1M tokens depending on model size and latency needs. We'll include margin targets (target gross margin >60% on feature-level) and show where inference cost is the limiting factor.

- For the Wed call agenda:
  1) Walk the numbers in the sheet (10-20 min)
  2) Hosted vs Dedicated: break-even analysis at 6/12/24 month horizons (15-20 min)
  3) CAC payback and $/feature sensitivity (15 min)
  4) Action items & SOW/T&C ask (10 min)

Jamie — if you can confirm budget range and whether procurement needs a preliminary redline review on the SOW, that would help us prep.

See you Wed 10:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>

Adding to HubSpot deal DC-2026-007 and will attach the unit-econ sheet and SOW after the call.

-Rishi
